# test/fixtures/90.05-payroll.ct — provenance and reconstruction notes

*Created 2026-08-02. This is the re-keyed card deck of the J28-6169 Appendix
90.05 sample payroll program. It is the only surviving COMTRAN program with
known-correct output: the printed report, J28-6169 PDF p. 217.*

## What this file is

A reconstruction of the **source card deck** of the 90.05 sample problem.
Since 2026-08-03 the authoritative form is the punch-level canon file
`90.05-payroll.ctd`, generated once from the re-keyed text and verified by
round trip; `90.05-payroll.ct` is now its generated text mirror (decision
D0.5; format in `docs/design/deck-format.md`). The mirror renders one line
per card, card columns 1–72 significant, columns 73–80 (identification)
blank throughout and trimmed along with all trailing blanks. 293 cards:

| Cards | Content |
|---|---|
| 1 | `*COMPILE` control card |
| 2–179 | `*DATA` header + 177 data description cards (statements 1,00–172,00; five entries occupy two cards each — see *Continuation cards* below) |
| 180–195 | `*ENVIRONMENT` header + 15 environment cards (statements 173,00–186,00; the PAYFILE FILE specification occupies two cards) |
| 196–293 | `*PROCEDURE` header + 97 procedure cards (statements 187,00–229,00) |

## Sources and method

- **Character content** is taken from the verified transcription
  `comtran-manuals/J28-6169/90.05-sample-program.md` (compilation listing,
  PDF pp. 192–197), which reproduces card body columns 7–72 per [J 02.02.01].
- **Column layout** was *measured from the page scans*
  (`comtran-manuals/J28-6169/images/page-192.png` … `page-197.png`) by
  pixel-level analysis: per-page calibration of printer pitch (~9.1 px/char at
  the scans' resolution) against structurally fixed columns (Level 23–24, Type
  25–30, Quantity 31–35, Mode 36, Justify 37, Description 38–71, per [F p. 65] /
  J 02.06.01), then per-line mapping of every ink group to card columns.
  The transcription's own spacing is normalized and was **not** relied on for
  layout.
- Content was verified after assembly by a whitespace-insensitive
  character-stream comparison of the whole deck against the transcription
  (identical except item 1 below, which the 2026-08-05 erratum has since
  corrected in the transcription).

## What is deliberately NOT in the deck

The deck holds card content only. Everything in the listing that is compiler
output stays out:

- the page headers;
- the `CTC`, `CTD`, and `CTE` compiler-phase markers, printed on-line at phase
  entry ([J 05.03]);
- the `NO ERRORS...` message;
- the statement-number column and the LOC column;
- the compiler-generated `GN)nnn` names — "names generated by the Compiler ...
  shown in the name field of Procedure statements or Data entries unnamed by the
  programmer" ([J 02.02.01]). Those entries' name fields are blank on the cards,
  as punched.

## Layout facts established from the scans

- **Serial columns 1–6 are blank** on every card: the listing's serial column
  is empty throughout.
- All three division headers have their asterisk in **column 7**. An earlier
  reading put `*PROCEDURE`'s asterisk in column 8; cell-boundary re-measurement
  (2026-08-03, adversarial verification of M1) shows its `*` in the same
  character cell as the `G` of `GN)000` on the next line — and `GN)nnn` prints
  in the name field, card column 7 ([J 02.02.01]). `*ENVIRONMENT` aligns with
  `INPUTMASTER` and `*DATA` with `MASTER` the same way, and F is explicit
  ("the asterisk is in Column 7", [F p. 65]). The deck was corrected to column 7
  on 2026-08-03.
- The `*COMPILE` card is an earlier-format counterpart of the [J 02.01] `$CMPLE`
  card. It reads `*COMPILE` from column 7, the option `LIST` at column 16, and
  the secondary identifier `CT PUBLICATIONS` at column 55. Those two field
  positions match the documented `$CMPLE` fields ([J 02.01.01]–02.01.02). The
  measurement is anchored on the console `CTC` print at print position 1. The
  identifier's start carries ±1 column uncertainty.
- Data names are indented freely within the Name field (7–22); indent is
  hierarchical but not uniform (e.g. MASTER's subfields step 9/11/13 by level,
  DETAIL/CHECK/PAYRECORD subfields step 8/9, TABLE.ITEM's subfields are flush
  at 7). Several names end flush at column 22 with the level abutting at
  23–24 (`EMPLOYEE.NUMBER02`, `CNTRLCHARSECLIN02`, `ENDFRSTLINE` + `02RCDMRK`).
- Levels are punched as in the listing: single digits right-justified in
  column 24, two-digit forms `01`/`02`/`03` in 23–24 (both styles appear;
  [J 02.05.01] allows either).
- TABLE's constant-only continuation cards (statements 145–167, odd ones)
  carry their quoted constant starting in **column 38** (Description field),
  not aligned under the preceding pictorial's constant.
- `TABLE.ITEM`'s repetition count `12` sits right-justified in Quantity
  columns 34–35.
- Procedure statements: procedure-names start at the name margin (column 7);
  sentence text and continuation lines start at column 13 except statement
  187's operand continuation lines (column 18) and lines whose first word
  follows a long name. Statement 208's first line runs exactly through
  column 72.

## Reconstruction decisions (unrecoverable from the listing)

1. **Column-72 continuation character = `X`** on the six two-card entries
   (statements 3, 21, 22, 103, 107 — name continued; statement 181 — FILE
   options continued). A non-blank column 72 is required for continuation
   ([F p. 84]; [J 02.06.01.01]), but the processor "replaces the contents of
   column 72 with a blank in Data and Environment lines" ([J 02.03.01] §2.c),
   so the listing cannot show which character was punched. Any non-blank
   character is equivalent to the language.
2. **Far-right spacing of long free-form procedure lines** carries ±1-space
   uncertainty: the scans show a mild progressive horizontal stretch (~1.5%
   per column), corrected during measurement, but word gaps beyond ~column 60
   rest on local inter-word measurements. All gaps were resolved to the
   best-fit integer; none is semantically significant.
3. Interior spacing of the two report-header literals (statements 80, 82) is
   now *measured*, not just length-derived: `DEPARTMENT` starts at column 55
   ⇒ ten spaces after the opening quote; `TOTALS` starts at column 46 ⇒ one
   leading and five trailing spaces. Closing quotes (columns 66 and 57) are
   forced by the A(21)/A(12) field lengths.

## Transcription errata found during re-keying

The manual conversions are read-only, so each item below needed Jack's
authorization against `90.05-sample-program.md`. All four were authorized
and applied on 2026-08-05.

1. **Statement 43,00: the punched name is `CNTRLCHARSECLIN` (15 characters),
   not `CNTRLCHARSECLINE`.** The scan (p. 192) shows `CNTRLCHARSECLIN02` with
   the level `02` abutting directly after the final `N` in columns 23–24; a
   16-character name would end in column 23 and could not abut a 23–24 level
   field. Confirmed at high zoom and by pixel measurement (17 contiguous
   character cells from column 8). The deck uses `CNTRLCHARSECLIN`.
   *Applied 2026-08-05.* The correction drops the spurious `E` and keeps the
   level in its transcribed print column. It does not close the name-to-level
   gap, which the print does not have: the level prints in a fixed column that
   a 15-character name reaches exactly, so the gap is the transcription's
   column flattening, not a spacing slip. M1-15 already rules the
   transcription unusable for column evidence, so no erratum is needed.
2. **Statement 203, line 2 reads `1.5 -20)`** (no space between the minus and
   `20`), where the transcription printed `1.5 - 20)`. Confirmed by grid
   overlay at p. 196. *Applied 2026-08-05.*
3. **Word spacing at seven sites in Procedure and Environment text.**
   *Applied 2026-08-05.* Pages 195 to 197 were measured at a fitted pitch of
   9.32 px per character. One space measures 11 to 14 px between ink; two
   spaces measure 22 to 25 px. The two ranges do not overlap, so each site
   below is decided, not estimated.

   | Statement | Site | The print | The conversion held | The deck held |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 182 | after `SPECIFPAYFILE,` | one space | one space | **two spaces** |
   | 182 | after `OPENW,` | one space | none | one space |
   | 187 | `CALL` to `(MASTER` | one space | two spaces | one space |
   | 198 | after `HIGH.VALUE,` | two spaces | one space | two spaces |
   | 199 | after `MOVE` | two spaces | one space | two spaces |
   | 199 | after `FILES,` | two spaces | one space | two spaces |
   | 220 | after `BONDENOMINATION,` | two spaces | one space | two spaces |

   Six sites corrected the conversion. The first site corrected **the deck**:
   card 191 carried one space too many, so `UNIT1` stood in card column 41
   where the print puts it in column 40. `test/goldens/90.05-payroll.listing`
   echoed that card and was regenerated with it.

   Two limits on the conversion correction. It changes the gaps inside a card
   body and nothing else: statement 187's `(MASTER` still does not align with
   the `(DETAIL` below it in the transcription, although the print aligns
   both in card column 18. Column evidence comes from the scans (M1-15), not
   from this text. And it stops at the conversion: the language definition
   reproduces the corrected spacing in its verbatim listing excerpt (§9.4),
   but its inline examples of `CLOSE ALL FILES, STOP RUN.` and
   `HIGH.VALUE, GO TO HIGH.DETAIL.` stay single-spaced, because they show
   syntax, and the gap width carries no meaning to the compiler.

   An earlier form of this entry read a double space at both statement-182
   sites and closed with an uncounted remark about the name-margin gaps. The
   measurement refutes the first reading. The name margin holds the listing's
   fixed name, level and type fields, where item 1 above already shows the
   transcription flattens columns; a gap there is not evidence of a punch.

   Item 4 below records two sites this pass missed.
4. **Word spacing at two more sites in statement 193.** *Applied 2026-08-05.*
   The print reads `MOVE 'M' TO ERRORTYPE,  MOVE MASTER DAT  TO`, with two
   spaces after `ERRORTYPE,` and two between `DAT` and `TO`. The conversion
   held one space at each. The deck already held two at each, so this
   correction touches the conversion alone. No golden and no test changes.

   | Site | The print | The conversion held | The deck held |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | after `ERRORTYPE,` | two spaces | one space | two spaces |
   | after `DAT` | two spaces | one space | two spaces |

   The measurement uses item 3's grid. On PDF p. 195 the second `MOVE` starts
   at x=986, where two spaces predict 986 and one space predicts 976. Its
   blank run measures 23 px, inside item 3's two-space band of 22 to 25 px.
   The `TO` starts at x=1146, where two spaces predict 1144 and one space
   predicts 1135.

   Two sites on the same card stay uncorrected, because they are column
   evidence and not word spacing: the print puts one space after the sequence
   number `71500` and two after the label `HIGH.DETAIL.`, where the conversion
   pads both fields to a fixed column. Item 3's second limit already covers
   this, and M1-15 rules the transcription unusable for column evidence.

   A card-by-card comparison of the deck against the conversion found these
   two sites. A throwaway script did that pass. It covered 98 of the 112
   Environment and Procedure cards, and a hand check covered the other 14.
   Statement 193 was the only divergence. The Data Division is out of the
   comparison, because the listing prints those entries in its own fixed
   columns.

   *Amended 2026-08-06.* `test/deck_conversion_test.dart` now holds the
   comparison as a standing test, and it reaches all 112 cards. The 14 cards
   the script left to a hand check were not 14. Six cards need a rule that
   the script did not have, and the other eight need none:

   | Cards | Why a plain word match misses them | The rule |
   |---|---|---|
   | 4 | The listing glues a generated name to the first punched word, as in `GN)000CALL` | A generated name fills the name margin, columns 7 to 12, so text that starts in column 13 abuts it |
   | 2 | Two listing lines carry the same words, `GET MASTER, AT END DO END.OF.MASTERS.` | Accept a duplicate when the candidate lines agree on their blank runs |

   The standing test compares 438 blank runs and finds no divergence. It
   excludes a blank run inside a fixed field, because the printer sets that
   run and no punch decides it: the Environment name and type fields,
   columns 7 to 30, and a Procedure margin name.

## Using the deck

- Expected end-to-end output: the printed payroll register, J28-6169 PDF
  p. 217 (see roadmap milestone M6 in `docs/HANDOVER.md`).
- The deck is the M1 lexer/card-reader test input (columns model: serial 1–6,
  name margin 7–12/name field 7–22, text/description to 71–72, continuation
  column 72).

## The generated job deck (90.05-payroll-job.ctd)

`90.05-payroll-job.ctd` is a generated sibling, not part of the artifact:
the 293 cards above plus one `*FINISH` card (columns 7–13). **The *FINISH
card is a reconstruction.** The 1962 listing echoes no *FINISH, and the
re-keyed artifact holds attested card content only; a complete job needs the
terminator ([J 02.01.02]), so decision D11.3 adds it in this separate file, as
D9.14 provides. The compiler's acceptance command compiles the job deck. The
artifact stays 293 cards; `test/driver_test.dart` asserts the count, and the
raw artifact compiled alone draws message 132 by design.
